name: OR-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Suzanne Bonamici running with large financial edge
Republican challenger raised only ~$4,500 with no outside support
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~96%
model.rationale: Bonamici holds a D+20 seat, has over $570,000 on hand, and faces a challenger who has raised almost nothing, while markets price her near-certain to win. No polls or expert ratings contradict the fundamentals, so the forecast stays at a roughly 25-point Democratic margin.
model.watch: A surprise wave-level Republican environment or an unexpected well-funded challenger entry could narrow the margin, though a seat this lean is very unlikely to flip.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Oregon's 1st District is a solidly Democratic Portland-suburban seat with a 20-point Democratic partisan lean. Incumbent Suzanne Bonamici is running for another term and holds a decisive financial advantage, with over $570,000 in cash on hand after raising more than $800,000 this cycle.

Republican Barbara Kahl has raised only about $4,500 and reports just a few hundred dollars on hand, with no outside spending on either side. No general-election polls or expert ratings are available, but prediction markets put Bonamici's win probability around 96%. The race is rated Safe Democratic.
